plan.planning_summary: Refining route_02 (chirped stack) based on prior iteration results showing score decline from 0.7998 to 0.7148 when monotonicity constraints were added. Three complementary routes proposed: (1) Quarter-wave seeded optimization with ±15% jitter per feedback directives, (2) Reduced 20-layer periodic stack to test over-constraint hypothesis, (3) Explicit two-band center design targeting 375nm and 1350nm simultaneously. All routes maintain 30-layer maximum, HfO2/SiO2 materials, fused silica substrate, and normal incidence unpolarized illumination.

routes.title: Quarter-Wave Seeded Stack with ±15% Thickness Jitter and Expanded Bounds
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Starting from quarter-wave optical thickness seeds at band centers (375nm UV, 1350nm SWIR) with ±15% random jitter will escape local minima that constrained the chirped parameterization, while expanding thickness bounds to 500nm provides additional design freedom without violating fabrication limits.
routes.design_principle: Quarter-wave stack theory provides optimal reflectance per layer pair; jittering seeds allows optimizer to find non-quarter-wave improvements while maintaining physical intuition. Evidence shows quarter-wave stacks maximize reflectivity for minimum layer count when optical thickness equals λ/4.
routes.proposed_topology: exactly 6 alternating HfO2/SiO2 pairs (12 finite layers)
design_variables: 30 individual layer thicknesses (nm), each independently optimizable
soft_objectives: Maximize average transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band
Maximize average reflectance in 300-450 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: Individual layer thickness bounds: 20-500 nm (expanded from 450 nm per feedback)
Outermost SiO2 layer >= 200 nm for environmental durability
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack theory: reflectivity maximizes when layer optical thickness equals λ/4
Outermost low-index layer improves environmental durability per multi-wavelength HR evidence
expected_advantages: Better convergence than monotonicity-constrained chirp due to unconstrained thickness space
Quarter-wave seeds provide physically meaningful starting point
Expanded bounds allow thicker layers for broader UV reflection band
known_risks: May converge to local minimum if jitter amplitude insufficient
30 independent variables may require more optimization iterations
No monotonicity constraint could produce non-fabricable thickness profiles
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 30-layer HfO2/SiO2 multilayer coating on fused silica substrate at normal incidence with unpolarized illumination. Stack topology: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | ... (alternating, 15 bilayer pairs, 30 total finite layers) | Fused Silica. Initialize layer thicknesses using quarter-wave optical thickness at 375 nm for HfO2 and SiO2 layers in the first 10 pairs (UV reflector region), and at 1350 nm for remaining 5 pairs (SWIR transmitter region). Apply ±15% uniform random jitter to all seed thicknesses. Set individual layer thickness optimization bounds: 20 nm minimum, 500 nm maximum. Constrain outermost SiO2 layer thickness >= 200 nm. Optimize all 30 layer thicknesses simultaneously to maximize average transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band and maximize average reflectance in 300-450 nm band. Use gradient-based optimizer with increased initial population sampling density (2x baseline). Evaluate spectrum from 300-1700 nm at 5 nm resolution. Topology realization override: disregard any symbolic repeat count, range, or ellipsis above and use exactly 6 alternating HfO2/SiO2 pairs (12 finite layers). Optimize only continuous physical thicknesses; the task compiler must fully expand every finite layer. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 300-450 nm, 1000-1700 nm. soft objectives: high transmission in 1000-1700 nm; high reflection in 300-450 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: low transmission in 300-450 nm; low reflection in 1000-1700 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layer count <= 30; materials restricted to HfO2 and SiO2.
routes.revision_reason: Applied feedback directives: ±15% jitter to quarter-wave seeds, expanded upper thickness bound from 450 nm to 500 nm, increased population sampling density. Removed monotonicity constraint that reduced score from 0.7998 to 0.7148 in prior iteration.

routes.title: 20-Layer Periodic Stack to Test Over-Constraint Hypothesis
routes.scientific_hypothesis: The 30-layer constraint may be over-constraining the design space, causing optimization difficulty. A 20-layer periodic stack with quarter-wave seeding will test whether fewer layers with more thickness freedom per layer achieves comparable or better spectral separation.
routes.design_principle: Evidence shows high-reflectance stacks can achieve >99.99% reflectance with optimized layer counts; reducing layer count may improve optimizer convergence by reducing dimensionality while maintaining sufficient optical degrees of freedom.

design_variables: 20 individual layer thicknesses (nm), each independently optimizable

Achieve comparable target score to 30-layer designs with fewer layers
manufacturing_considerations: Total layer count exactly 20 (well within 30-layer limit)
Outermost SiO2 layer >= 200 nm for environmental durability
Reduced layer count improves fabrication yield and stress management
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack reflectivity scales with layer pair count; 10 pairs may suffice for dichroic separation
Global optimization with bounded thickness effective for 4-layer configurations per evidence; scaling to 20 layers tests dimensionality limits
expected_advantages: Lower dimensionality (20 vs 30 variables) may improve optimizer convergence
Tests whether 30 layers is necessary or over-constrained
known_risks: May not achieve sufficient UV reflectance with only 10 bilayer pairs
Reduced design freedom may limit spectral shaping capability
Could produce lower target score than 30-layer designs

routes.title: Two-Band Center Quarter-Wave Design with Explicit Spectral Targets
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Explicitly designing quarter-wave stacks at both band centers (375 nm for UV reflection, 1350 nm for SWIR transmission) with optimized transition region will achieve better spectral separation than chirped or monotonic approaches by directly targeting the physical mechanism of band formation.
routes.design_principle: Multi-wavelength HR evidence shows simultaneous optimization at discrete wavelengths with bandwidth specifications achieves >99.99% reflectance. Applying this to dichroic design: UV band uses short-wavelength quarter-wave stack, SWIR band uses long-wavelength anti-reflection design.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | (SiO2 | HfO2) x 5 (UV reflector) | (HfO2 | SiO2) x 10 (transition/matching) | Fused Silica substrate. Total 30 finite layers. Note: First section starts with SiO2 for UV quarter-wave stack on air side, outermost is SiO2 for durability.
design_variables: 30 individual layer thicknesses (nm), grouped into UV reflector (10 layers), transition region (20 layers)
soft_objectives: Maximize average reflectance in 300-450 nm band (target: >95%)
Maximize average transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band (target: >90%)
manufacturing_considerations: UV reflector section uses quarter-wave at 375 nm as seed
theory_basis: Multi-wavelength HR optimization at discrete wavelengths with bandwidth specs achieves high reflectance
Quarter-wave stack theory for reflectance maximization
Transition region design for impedance matching between UV reflector and SWIR passband
expected_advantages: Direct physical targeting of band centers may improve spectral separation
Explicit UV reflector section ensures high reflection in 300-450 nm
Transition region optimization reduces passband ripple
known_risks: May create sharp transition causing ripple in 450-1000 nm region
Quarter-wave at both centers may conflict (375 nm QW vs 1350 nm QW thickness ratio ~3.6x)
Complex topology may be harder to optimize than simple periodic stack
